definition_context: The embedded infinite natural differentiability index denotes all finite derivative orders, not analyticity.

Poincare.Admissible μ f means that f, its squared centered value, and its squared genuine gradient norm are all integrable. Poincare.variance is the integral of the squared centered value; Poincare.dirichletEnergy is the integral of the squared gradient norm.
cases.statement:
example
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (μ : Measure E) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (C : ℝ)
    (hLSI : ∀ (v : E → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ∞ v → HasCompactSupport v →
      (∫ x, (v x)^2 * Real.log ((v x)^2) ∂μ) -
        (∫ x, (v x)^2 ∂μ) * Real.log (∫ x, (v x)^2 ∂μ) ≤
      2 * C * ∫ x, ‖gradient v x‖^2 ∂μ)
    (f : E → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) (hs : HasCompactSupport f) :
    Poincare.Admissible μ f ∧ Poincare.variance μ f ≤ C * Poincare.dirichletEnergy μ f

definition_context: withDensity constructs the measure with the given nonnegative extended-real density relative to the reference measure. ENNReal.ofReal sends negative inputs to zero. The real value of an extended-real divergence is an ordinary divergence only when finiteness is known.
cases.statement:
example
    {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (f : X → ℝ) (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) {M : ℝ}
    (hbound : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, |f x| ≤ M) (hcenter : (∫ x, f x ∂μ) = 0) :
    let ν := fun e : ℝ => μ.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (1 + e * f x))
    (∀ᶠ e : ℝ in 𝓝 (0 : ℝ),
      IsProbabilityMeasure (ν e) ∧ _root_.InformationTheory.klDiv (ν e) μ < ⊤) ∧
    (fun e : ℝ => (_root_.InformationTheory.klDiv (ν e) μ).toReal -
      e ^ 2 * ((∫ x, f x ^ 2 ∂μ) / 2)) =o[𝓝 (0 : ℝ)] (fun e : ℝ => e ^ 2)
